decisions.quote: However, empirical findings on the distinguishability of these two knowledge components, and their relationship with student outcomes, are mixed. In this replication and extension study, we explore these issues, drawing on evidence from a multi-year study of over 200 fourth- and fifth-grade US teachers.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist at the listed paths. The supplied source text is a publisher preview containing only the title, abstract, endnotes, and reference list, omitting the main text body. The abstract and endnotes characterize the work as a replication and extension study examining the dimensionality of teacher content knowledge (CK) and pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) / mathematical knowledge for teaching (MKT) and their contribution to student learning, without naming the specific prior study or studies being replicated. The reference list includes shipped row input_row_index 29 (Copur-Gencturk, Tolar, Jacobson, & Fan, 2018, DOI 10.1177/0022487118761860) as well as multiple other empirical studies of CK/PCK/MKT dimensionality and student achievement (e.g., Hill, Schilling, & Ball, 2004; Hill, Rowan, & Ball, 2005; Krauss et al., 2008; Baumert et al., 2010; Kleickmann et al., 2013, 2015; Campbell et al., 2014). Without the primary article body, the available evidence does not settle whether the replication target is already represented by shipped row 29 or includes another specific study from the reference list.
